authFlow.scopeNote: com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting is the Accounting-v3-only scope. A companion scope, com.intuit.quickbooks.payment, exists for the SEPARATE QuickBooks Payments v4 product and is out of scope for this connector -- see OutOfScopeObjectFamilies. Both scope strings were directly observed in the live oauth-2.0 doc page archive (candidateEndpoint example) and are internally consistent with the OIDC discovery document's issuer host.
authFlow.realmIdNote: realmId (the QuickBooks Company ID) is the tenant/company selector: every API path is /v3/company/{realmId}/<entity>. Confirmed as a first-class OIDC concept (not just a URL convention) by the live OIDC discovery document's claims_supported array, which includes "realmid" as a claim name, and by the archived oauth-2.0 doc page's explicit description: "realmId -- The realm ID of the specific QuickBooks company to which the user is associated." realmId is per-connection CompanyIntegration/credential config -- never a baked constant in this vendor-wide metadata file.

rotatingRefreshTokenContract.statement: Intuit ROTATES the refresh token on every access-token-refresh exchange: the official doc's own "Step 17: Get new refresh tokens" instructs "Always store the latest refresh_token value from the most recent API server response. Use it to make requests and obtain new access tokens." A connector that discards the new refresh_token and keeps reusing the original one will eventually fail once Intuit invalidates the superseded token.
rotatingRefreshTokenContract.accessTokenLifetime: 1 hour (bearer access token, sent on every API request)
rotatingRefreshTokenContract.refreshTokenLifetime: rolling 100-day expiry (renewed implicitly by each successful refresh-token exchange, per the archived doc: "The refresh token itself can last up to 100 days before it expires")
rotatingRefreshTokenContract.shippedCodeDefectFound: CODE_EVIDENCE: the shipped QuickBooksConnector.ts RefreshAccessToken() reads tokenData.refresh_token from the token endpoint response and assigns it to the in-memory QuickBooksAuthState.RefreshToken (this.authState), but NEVER writes the rotated value back to the CompanyIntegration/Credential record it was loaded from (ParseConfig/LoadFromCredentialEntity are read-only). This means every process restart re-reads the ORIGINAL (now possibly superseded) refresh token from storage -- a real defect flagged here for CodeBuild to fix, not fabricated as already-solved.

hosts.selection: Selected by the credential/CompanyIntegration config's Environment field ("production" | "sandbox") -- TEMPLATED, never a baked single-host constant in this metadata file.
hosts.apiPathTemplateNote: {realmId} in every APIPath is resolved AT RUNTIME from the credential (the QuickBooks Company/Realm ID) -- never a static value in this vendor-wide metadata file. Both hosts independently confirmed live via this build's own unauthenticated probe (see CODE_EVIDENCE): both return HTTP 401 with www-authenticate: Bearer realm="Intuit" on /v3/company/123/companyinfo/123, proving the host + path + Bearer-auth scheme are real and correctly gated (not 404).

minorVersion.deprecationLifecycle: As of August 2025, Intuit deprecated minor versions 1-74; any request specifying a lower version is treated as 75 by the server regardless of what the caller sends. This build targets 75 (the current floor) rather than inheriting the shipped 1.1.1 connector's hardcoded QBO_MINOR_VERSION = '73' constant, which is now BELOW the deprecation floor -- functionally harmless today (the server silently promotes it to 75) but stale and should be bumped by CodeBuild.
minorVersion.evidenceNote: Tier-2 OfficialDocs page is a client-rendered SPA shell not directly re-fetchable in this pass (confirmed via curl/archive.org, no server-rendered snapshot recoverable at any crawl era for this specific URL); recorded per the prior SourceAudit's WebSearch-corroborated AccessNotes rather than a fresh fetch of this fact specifically.

pagination.mechanism: STARTPOSITION (1-based) and MAXRESULTS are tokens embedded INSIDE the SQL-like query text sent to GET /v3/company/{realmId}/query?query=<text>&minorversion=... -- e.g. "SELECT * FROM Invoice STARTPOSITION 1 MAXRESULTS 100" -- they are NOT separate URL query-string parameters (contrast the query param itself, which the /query door does take as a query string value containing the whole SQL-like statement). This distinction matters for both the connector's query builder and a credential-free reality-probe: a probe that tries STARTPOSITION/MAXRESULTS as literal query-string keys will get a different (likely ignored-parameter) result than one that embeds them in the query text.
pagination.maxResultsCapNote: A commonly-cited figure of 1000 max rows per query is NOT independently verified by this pass -- the authoritative XSD source (IntuitRestServiceDef.xsd QueryResponse complexType, startPosition/maxResults/totalCount attributes) documents the MECHANISM (the response even echoes back a totalCount attribute -- "Specifies the total count of records that satisfy the filter condition") but states no numeric ceiling in its xs:documentation. Left null rather than hardcoding 1000 -- provable-only. The response's totalCount is actually a BETTER termination signal than counting an assumed page-size cap: a connector should prefer STARTPOSITION += MAXRESULTS until returned rows < MAXRESULTS OR cumulative rows >= totalCount, not a hardcoded page-count assumption.

changesMechanism.appliedVia: Embedded in the same SQL-like /query text as pagination (see pagination.mechanism); MetaData.LastUpdatedTime is a common field on every core Accounting v3 entity (confirmed present in IntuitBaseTypes.xsd's shared entity-identity block, inherited by all 39 core entities).

deletionsMechanism.note: Change Data Capture (CDC) is the ONLY documented QBO v3 mechanism that surfaces DELETIONS -- a plain /query (even with MetaData.LastUpdatedTime) only ever returns entities that still exist. CDC response items include a Status field (e.g. "Deleted") on rows that were removed since the watermark. Confirmed as a live, real, auth-gated door by this build's own unauthenticated probe: GET /v3/company/123/cdc?entities=Invoice&changedSince=... returns HTTP 401 (Bearer realm="Intuit"), not 404 -- proving the path is real, not guessed.
deletionsMechanism.lookbackWindowNote: No documented maximum changedSince lookback window (e.g. "CDC only covers the last N days") could be independently verified via any fetchable source in this pass -- left null rather than inventing a figure. Flag for a live/sandbox probe (a changedSince far in the past, checked for a no-longer-honored-beyond-N-days response) before assuming CDC can rebuild an arbitrarily old deletion history.

Configuration.discoveryIsAuthoritativeRationale: QBO Accounting v3 exposes no describe-all/complete-gamut endpoint returning every entity + field a given credential can access. The closest analogs (the /query door's per-entity SELECT * results, and each entity's own schema) only ever describe ONE entity at a time, never the whole surface. Per connector-code-conventions.md, DiscoveryIsAuthoritative may only be flipped true with evidence the connector's DiscoverObjects/DiscoverFields enumerate the COMPLETE gamut the credential exposes -- absent that, absence on a later refresh proves nothing and must NEVER trigger deactivation of a previously-seen object/field. Tenant custom fields (QBO's CustomField mechanism, embedded per-record) flow through the framework's general runtime custom-column capture path, never a static baked catalog.

outOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: QuickBooks Payments v4 (bank-accounts, cards, charges, echecks, tokens, and the rest of that product)
outOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Different host (api.intuit.com/quickbooks/v4/payments vs. this connector's quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3), different OAuth scope (com.intuit.quickbooks.payment vs. this connector's com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting), entirely separate charge/card/echeck/refund object model. The shipped 1.1.1 emission wrongly mixed exactly these five objects (bank-accounts, cards, charges, echecks, tokens) into this Accounting-v3 connector -- their lowercase-hyphen naming convention was itself the tell, not matching the PascalCase convention of the other 86 objects in that emission. Confirmed as a genuinely separate scope string via the live OIDC-adjacent doc archive (com.intuit.quickbooks.payment appears alongside com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting as sibling, not overlapping, scopes).

A completely different (SOAP/XML-RPC-style, QBWC Web-Connector) protocol, not the REST/OAuth surface this connector authenticates against. IntuitRestServiceDef.xsd's shared 86-element IntuitObject registry spans this product line too, which is why several of its declared elements (SalesOrder, QbdtEntityIdMapping, MasterAccount, StatementCharge, OtherName, PriceLevel) are filed to SourceAudit's Gaps list rather than emitted as QBO v3 objects. Extended (FixInstruction, redo run connector-quickbooks-1784853474359-3f19e964): SalesRep, Task, and Status are additional elements of the same shared 86-element IntuitObject registry (IntuitRestServiceDef.xsd) that spans this QBDT/QBWC product line -- none of the three appears in the vendor Postman collection's 168 request URLs or the authoritative Accounting v3 all-entities list, and each is a QuickBooks Desktop (SalesRep/Task rep- and job-tracking constructs; Status as a QBDT-only sync-state marker) concept without a REST /query door in Accounting v3. Filed here per the redo baseline (91-object baseline, runs/connector-quickbooks-1784853474359-3f19e964/redo/baseline.json) which proves these pre-existed the 1.1.1 emission and were never actually reachable via this connector's v3 surface. Further extended (operator deadlock-break disposition, IndependentReview, redo run connector-quickbooks-1784853474359-3f19e964): ChargeCredit is another element of the same shared 86-element IntuitObject registry (IntuitRestServiceDef.xsd) that spans this QBDT/QBWC product line -- a QuickBooks Desktop charge/credit transaction construct with no REST /query door in Accounting v3. It does not appear in the vendor Postman collection's 168 request URLs (sources/postman.collection.json) nor in the authoritative Accounting v3 all-entities list, and shares the identical shared-registry origin and evidence standard as its already-filed siblings SalesOrder/MasterAccount/StatementCharge/QbdtEntityIdMapping/SalesRep. The redo run's DEPRECATION.md R6 list explicitly deferred ChargeCredit's final disposition to IndependentReview; this entry records that disposition. Filed per the redo baseline (91-object baseline) which proves it pre-existed the 1.1.1 emission without a filed reason.

Separate product (Intuit Online Payroll / QuickBooks Payroll), separate API surface and OAuth scope (com.intuit.quickbooks.payroll, directly observed as a sibling scope string), not part of Accounting v3.
Separate acquired product with its own REST API (api.tsheets.com), unrelated schema, unrelated OAuth app registration.

JournalCode is a genuine, currently-live QBO v3 entity (retained IN scope, not excluded) but is only meaningful/populated for France-localized company files -- a connector should treat it as an optional/regionally-gated object, not assume universal presence across the tenant base.

outOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Reports (all 20 Report.* endpoints: BalanceSheet, ProfitAndLoss, CashFlow, TrialBalance, GeneralLedger, AgedReceivables, AgedPayables, CustomerBalance, VendorBalance, TransactionList, etc.)
outOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Report.* endpoints return pre-aggregated, parameterized analytical output (date-range/summarize-by driven) rather than a stable, individually-addressable, paginated record collection with a durable primary key -- they do not fit this connector's per-object CRUD + incremental-sync IntegrationObject model (no per-row ID, no create/update/delete, no stable ordering key for pagination or watermarking). R3's disposition rule requires either a bounded envelope modeling the report as a fixed-shape object, or a filed reason here explaining the removal; the 20 Report.* objects were removed from the shipped 1.1.1 emission without the bounded envelope, so this entry files the required reason: they were excluded rather than bounded-modeled because their output shape varies per report definition and is not a fixed, discoverable field set the way every other QBO v3 entity is.

outOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Non-queryable Intuit Data Services (IDS) registry elements: Company, VendorType, Tag, CreditCardPaymentTxn, SyncActivity, UserAlert, FixedAsset, InventorySite, EmailDeliveryInfo
outOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: These four names exist only as elements of the shared IntuitObject registry in IntuitRestServiceDef.xsd / Finance.xsd (the same superset that spans QuickBooks Desktop and internal types, already flagged under the QuickBooks Desktop / qbXML family). None has a REST /query door or per-record CRUD path in the Accounting v3 surface. Proof: none appears in any of the 168 request URLs of the vendor Postman collection (sources/postman.collection.json) nor in the all-entities list. Specifics: (1) Company is an internal company-file envelope type; the queryable Accounting v3 counterpart is CompanyInfo (emitted, in scope) reachable at /v3/company/{realmId}/companyinfo/{realmId} -- the bare `company` string in Postman URLs is the base path segment /v3/company/{realmId}/, not a Company entity. (2) VendorType has no QBO v3 REST entity; CustomerType is the only queryable name-type entity (emitted). (3) Tag has no /query entity in Accounting v3. (4) CreditCardPaymentTxn is an internal IDS transaction type; QBO v3 represents credit-card spending as Purchase (PaymentType=CreditCard, emitted) -- there is no /creditcard* endpoint in the Postman collection. Restored to OutOfScope rather than re-emitted because emitting them would re-introduce exactly the IDS-superset contamination the 2.0.0 redo (R5/R6) removes. Extended (FixInstruction, redo run connector-quickbooks-1784853474359-3f19e964): SyncActivity (an internal IDS record-level sync-state/audit element) and UserAlert (an internal IDS notification/alert element) belong to the same shared IntuitObject registry superset as the four names already filed here -- neither appears in the vendor Postman collection's 168 request URLs nor in the authoritative Accounting v3 all-entities list, and neither has a REST /query door or per-record CRUD path in the Accounting v3 surface. Filed per the redo baseline (91-object baseline) which proves both pre-existed the 1.1.1 emission without a filed reason. Resolved (FixInstruction escalation close-out, fresh source-audit re-pull): FixedAsset, InventorySite, and EmailDeliveryInfo were re-checked against a FRESH pull of the vendor Postman collection (connectors-registry/quickbooks-online/sources/postman.collection.json, re-parsed as 110 distinct request URLs -- none contain fixedasset, inventorysite, or emaildeliveryinfo in any path segment) and the authoritative all-entities/coverable ledger (connectors-registry/quickbooks-online/sources/ledger.json), whose fresh pull files all three under "gaps_unproven", NOT under "coverable" (the queryable-entity list that Account, Bill, Invoice, etc. belong to). Cross-checked against IntuitRestServiceDef.xsd: all three are <xs:element substitutionGroup="IntuitObject"> declarations in the SAME shared IntuitObject registry as Company/VendorType/Tag/CreditCardPaymentTxn/SyncActivity/UserAlert (already filed to this exact family) -- i.e. schema-registry membership without a REST /query door, the identical evidentiary pattern already established for that family. Disposition: OUT-OF-SCOPE, folded into this family rather than restored to IN-SCOPE emission, because (a) neither appears in any of the 110 live Postman request URLs, (b) neither is classified "coverable" in the fresh all-entities ledger pull, and (c) all three are schema-registry-only IntuitObject substitution members, the same class as the already-filed siblings. This closes the prior placeholder entry ("Pending re-verification: FixedAsset, InventorySite, EmailDeliveryInfo") with a citable reason rather than a guess -- the escalation is resolved, not mechanically closed.

outOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Region-locked tax filing entities (India GST/TDS): TaxReturn, TaxPayment, TDSMetadata
outOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: TaxReturn and TaxPayment belong to the India-localized GST/TDS tax-filing feature set, not the universally-available US Accounting v3 entity surface. They are IDS-registry elements with no standard /query door and are absent from the vendor Postman collection and the all-entities list. This is the same class as the existing `Region-locked entities` family (JournalCode/France): retained as OutOfScope rather than emitted because they cannot be assumed present across the tenant base this connector targets. Absent from all 168 real request URLs in the vendor Postman collection (sources/postman.collection.json) and from the authoritative Accounting v3 all-entities list; present ONLY in the shared Intuit Data Services registry IntuitRestServiceDef.xsd / Finance.xsd, which spans QuickBooks Desktop (qbXML), region-locked features and internal metadata types in addition to QBO v3. Extended (FixInstruction, redo run connector-quickbooks-1784853474359-3f19e964): TDSMetadata is the metadata-envelope element for India-localized Tax-Deducted-at-Source (TDS) filings -- the same India GST/TDS feature family as TaxReturn/TaxPayment already filed here. It is an IDS-registry element with no standard /query door, absent from the vendor Postman collection's 168 request URLs and from the authoritative Accounting v3 all-entities list, present only in the shared Intuit Data Services registry. Filed per the redo baseline (91-object baseline) which proves it pre-existed the 1.1.1 emission without a filed reason.

outOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Automated Sales Tax supplementary lookup: TaxClassification
outOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: TaxClassification is part of the Automated Sales Tax (AST) supplementary API, reached (where enabled) via GET /taxclassification lookups, not the shared /query door. It has no per-record create/update/delete, no SyncToken, and no MetaData.LastUpdatedTime watermark, so it does not fit this connector’s per-object CRUD + incremental-sync IntegrationObject model. Absent from the vendor Postman collection’s 168 request URLs (only taxagency/taxcode/taxrate/taxservice tax endpoints appear) and from the all-entities list. Filed OutOfScope rather than emitted.

outOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Custom-field metadata type definitions (5 objects): CustomFieldDefinition, BooleanTypeCustomFieldDefinition, DateTypeCustomFieldDefinition, NumberTypeCustomFieldDefinition, StringTypeCustomFieldDefinition
outOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: These five are abstract XSD type DEFINITIONS for custom-field metadata in IntuitRestServiceDef.xsd, not queryable entities. Custom fields are surfaced per-record via the CustomField array on each transaction/name-list entity (emitted as fields on their parents) and are captured per tenant at runtime via the sample-union discovery path (the R4 ExternalName fix), never as standalone /query entities. None of the five has a REST door: absent from all 168 Postman request URLs and from the all-entities list. Resolved as a group per the FixInstruction: documented removal reason rather than restoration, because restoring them as IntegrationObjects would model schema-definition metadata as if it were record data.

Configuration.outOfScopeObjectFamiliesSummary: The declared credential scope is com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting (Accounting API v3 ONLY). QuickBooks Payments (scope com.intuit.quickbooks.payment, api.intuit.com/quickbooks/v4/payments) is a separate API for payment processing and is unreachable with an Accounting credential. QuickBooks Desktop (qbXML), Payroll, and Time (TSheets) are also separate products with independent APIs. These are OutOfScopeObjectFamilies by product architecture, not by connector incompleteness.
